result:
I found 10 rules whose behaviour didn't match their docstring (or the common rules in the module docstring) and fixed all of them in `pricebook.py`. After the fixes, a script compared all 150 rules against what their docstrings describe and found no mismatches. It tested quantities 0–259 and a few larger values, a range of unit prices, and negative inputs.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 05, 16, 92 | The cap was applied to the base price, not the discount: `min(base, cap) * pct // 100` | Calculate the discount first, then cap it |
| 11 | Used `qty > 50`, so the discount didn't start at exactly 50 units | Changed to `qty >= 50` |
| 19, 80, 131 | Rounded the discount with `round(... / 100)` | Changed to floor division `// 100` |
| 30 | Rounded with `round(base * 15 / 100)` | Changed to floor division `// 100` |
| 77 | Marginal rule discounted all units | Now discounts only the units above the threshold: `(qty - 10) * unit * 12 // 100` |
| 82 | The cap only applied once the discount exceeded 200,000 won | Now always capped at 100,000 won |

STATUS: DONE
